items.text:
Are you interested in working with your clients utilizing Equine Assisted Psychotherapy but have no credentialing, horses, or facility in which to provide these services?🫩

I am looking for therapists who are paneled with Medicaid and have clients you think would benefit from Equine Assisted Psychotherapy. 😁 I am a therapist at Stable Grounds, Inc. in Middlebury and we are expanding our services to the community. All work is on the ground and we use both miniature and full-size horses. There is no riding involved. I would collaborate in these sessions with you utilizing Medicaid covered evidence-based modalities such as CBT, DBT, ACT, etc. The effectiveness of these interventions are enhanced through the use of horses.

EAP is a wonderful method for clients who struggle with ADHD, depression, anxiety, addictions, mood disorders etc and it works well for individuals of all ages. It is extremely effective for relationship building with couples and families. It is much more effective than talk therapy alone! Our facility is heated for the upcoming colder months and holidays - a time when our clients often need us most!

Please reach out to me if you have an interest or any questions regarding the potential benefits of EAP for your clients! 

Tails of Hope Counseling Services, LLC

The closer I get to finishing my BSW, the more possibilities I see for where I could take my career, and I honestly feel a little all over the place because I’m interested in so many of them.
Right now, I’m in the process of applying to add a Wellness Coach Certification Emphasis to my BSW for students who want to specialize in working with children and youth. Most of the requirements already align with what I’ve completed and the work I’m doing in my practicum, so I would only need one additional credit to earn it alongside my degree.

After my BSW, the plan is to complete an Advanced Standing MSW and work toward becoming an LCSW.

From there, I’m still figuring out exactly what I want my career to look like. I could see myself eventually working in private practice as a therapist, particularly with children, adolescents, and families. At the same time, I’ve been entertaining the idea of pursuing my JD part-time while earning my clinical hours toward LCSW licensure, with a focus on Child Welfare and Family Law.

Or maybe I eventually find a way to do both.

The intersection of mental health, child welfare, family systems, advocacy, and law genuinely interests me. I’m realizing that I don’t necessarily have to choose one path right now or have my entire career mapped out.

There are a lot of possibilities, and while I may feel a little all over the place trying to decide where I ultimately want to land, I’m excited to see where all of this takes me.

The closer I get to finishing my BSW, the more possibilities I see for where I could take my career, and I honestly feel a little all over the place because I’m interested in so many of them.

topComments.text: Get your MSW and your LCSW.  That will give you a wide open door to doing whatever you wish to do.  It led me to becoming an attorney and then, at age 60, coming back to being a therapist in private practice. (Covid was hard on family law attorneys).

items.text:
If you wondered what MIND Global Council is up to…. 

Research!  Not just any research-  research that will help to inform, advocate, and  help direct best practices in treating kids with PANS/PANDAS from a mental health lens.

More to come!  Get your popcorn ready and STAY TUNED!!

sharedPost.text:
This is the work behind what comes next.

MIND Global Council is currently examining five essential clinical questions in PANS/PANDAS mental health care, drawing on perspectives from more than 1,000 parents and clinicians internationally.

Our research is looking at:

- What PANS/PANDAS can look like from a mental health perspective
- Which psychotherapy approaches are perceived as most helpful across different symptom severity states
- When psychotherapy may be most appropriate relative to medical treatment
- How clinicians can better assess and recognize complex or fluctuating presentations
- What knowledge, skills, experience, and adaptations clinicians need to provide effective support

These findings are helping us identify priorities for evidence-informed clinical guidance, clinician training, and future research.

And this is only the beginning.

The goal is to translate what we learn into clear, practical mental health guidance for clinicians supporting individuals and families affected by PANS/PANDAS.

Research first. Clinical guidance to follow.

We’ll share more about each area of this work—and the guidance it informs—in the months ahead.

📣 SPONSORS NEEDED—and a very special shout-out to two of our newest
community sponsors! 💛 We are incredibly grateful to Creative Face Painting by Diana and DeliaMar Mega-Shop for stepping forward as community sponsors of the Speak Our Truth Project: Courage & Comedy Open Mic! 🎨🌻✨

🎨 Creative Face Painting by Diana is generously donating face-painting supplies to help us provide a fun, creative activity for the children and families attending our event.

🌻 DeliaMar Mega Shop is generously donating sunflowers to help us honor local mother and activist TaKisha Jacobs and the powerful advocacy legacy she helped build.

These thoughtful contributions will help us create a meaningful, welcoming, and family-friendly experience centered on creativity, connection, truth-telling, remembrance, and collective healing.

When local businesses invest in community events centered on child safety, they help create meaningful opportunities for youth, families, artists, advocates survivors, and community members to share their talents, speak their truths, build meaningful connections, and experience collective healing—all while advancing the greater mission of child-safety reform across Indiana.

📅 Saturday, October 17, 2026
⏰ 3:00–6:00 PM
📍 LangLab — South Bend 

This free, family-friendly event will feature local youth and community artists and speakers, courageous storytelling, poetry, music, comedy, creative expression, community resources, and a special tribute honoring TaKisha Jacobs.

Your sponsorship will directly support:
• Local youth and community artists and speakers
• Youth and community empowerment
• Uplifting voices, stories, talents, and truth
• Accessible creative activities and event supplies
• A welcoming space for connection, expression, justice, and healing
